title: Replace a fuse in an open, unplugged UK plug
instruction: Replace the fuse in the open, unplugged plug with the matching spare, then refit the removed carrier securely.
setup: A full-size moulded UK plug (64 × 45 mm, 65 g), disconnected from electricity, with its original 3 A cartridge seated in the spring terminals. The fuse carrier starts removed and upright in a 90 × 70 mm parts tray on a 25 mm riser. A matching 25.4 × 6.3 mm spare cartridge rests separately on an 18 × 18 × 12 mm wooden block. A plastic 85 × 70 mm parts dish has 16 mm sides. Both hands start open. README gives fixed coordinates and finger dimensions.
scoring: 1.0 if the old fuse is at least 40 mm outside its seat, the replacement is within 3 mm of its seat and aligned within 18°, and the carrier centre is within 2.5 mm and each face corner within 2.5 mm of the flush plane and aligned within 18°, with all parts retained for 3 seconds after both hands release. Removing the old fuse and seating the replacement earns 0.5; removing only the old fuse earns 0.25. Otherwise 0. Broken parts or parts dropped off the table score 0. Judge with the video, a ruler and angle template; no electrical test is required.
fidelity: Full-size passive spring terminals, cavity ends and carrier detents provide resistance and retention; stiffness and break loads are approximate. Contact-gated 12 N / 0.060 Nm native pinches approximate finger friction, releasing on opening or 8 mm slip. The real gripper receives reaction loads; clips can still break. No task pose is written. Opening the carrier is outside the timed task; no electrical test is claimed.
scores: Development draft; full-score native demo and paired baseline required.
context: Replacing a plug fuse requires extracting a retained cartridge, seating its replacement in spring clips and refitting the small carrier.
